dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "Everything tribal matter of importance will be written here. Every request you make may also be written down here. Everyone should check it regularly to avoid work delays."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "However, remember the ancient decrees, and know that words are only words. To win glory is to do deeds that should be written of, and wisdom is to write of wonders to be done."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Continue Reading

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "As the ancient sages say, all gifts come with a catch. Poison in a golden chalice is still poison, so all upstanding souls should stay on guard."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "Such is the nature of Spirit Immersion. Immersing oneself within a spiritual object without the requisite sensitivity is akin to submerging oneself in water before even learning to wade in it. How will that teach anyone to swim?"

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "It is precisely due to such great perils that this method was declared forbidden hundreds of years ago. Be careful not to endanger your own life."

dialogues.speaker: Granny Itztli's Message
dialogues.text: "So, listen up! I'll turn whoever gets themselves into trouble into stone and chuck them right outside my door. You'll be alive, at least — and I'll treat you once I'm in a better mood."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "You should know that tribal affairs contain certain taboos. Act in line with their strictures, and never do anything presumptuous."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "Remember to never strike with your hands anything made out of obsidian, especially the sacred pillar and the uncarved stone."

dialogues.speaker: Childish Handwriting
dialogues.text: "Correct. It's obsidian and imbued with mystical powers. If you hit it too hard, it'll lose that spiritual element."

dialogues.speaker: Unrefined Handwriting
dialogues.text: "I'm wetting myself laughing over here. What do you think obsidian is, some kind of precision gear? I'd say Granny Itztli just put a curse on the stone to stop other people from messing around with her materials..."

dialogues.speaker: Childish Handwriting
dialogues.text: "Oh, so you think you're all that just because you know Granny Itztli? What curse are you even talking about? You don't even understand the basic properties of obsidian, so what is there to even debate?"

dialogues.speaker: Unrefined Handwriting
dialogues.text: "The applications of sympathetic spellcraft... If you'd listened in class, you'd already know the principles behind taboos and curses."

dialogues.speaker: Another Person's Message
dialogues.text: "You two are squabbling like kids..."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "Clarification: There's no complicated reasoning behind this rule. Obsidian just has very sharp edges, and it'd be bad if anyone got cut."

dialogues.speaker: Hornshroom Augury Announcement
dialogues.text: "Notification: The store owner has decided to embark on a long voyage in search of inspiration and enlightenment. Thus Hornshroom Augury will hereby be permanently closed. Its reopening date will be announced at a later date."

dialogues.speaker: Silken Handwriting
dialogues.text: "I see, Master Chicome! You said before that we shouldn't take things literally, so what this means is that we should broaden our investment horizons into something like... tourism!"

dialogues.speaker: Hornshroom Augury
dialogues.text: "Get outta here, you!"

dialogues.speaker: Silken Handwriting
dialogues.text: "I understand. I'll get going! I'll make investments based on your oracle right away!"

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "Descendants of the Masters of the Night-Wind: The cries of the tribes echo through the night wind. Now is the time to recall the oath sworn by our ancestors."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "Whosoever has the strength to help a neighbor; whosoever knows sorcery, astronomy, or medicine must help the other tribes as our ancestors once did, that this pitch-black disaster brings not their fatal end."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "High Priestess Citlali has already departed. Follow her — we shall not fall behind!"

dialogues.speaker: Message
dialogues.text: "May I ask everyone: Are there any other good ways to relieve stress besides meditation? My mental load has been heavy recently, so I hope you can be generous with your advice. Many thanks."

dialogues.speaker: Another Person's Message
dialogues.text: "I've never seen a case like yours before. How about this: You go find Master Matla, who is a well-trained witch doctor. Tell him your symptoms, and he should be able to treat you."

dialogues.speaker: Message
dialogues.text: "Thanks for the suggestion, but I don't think that's going to work. You see, I *am* Master Matla."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "Descendants of the Masters of the Night-Wind: Just as the sun rises and sets, so too the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame draws ever-closer."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "May our tribal warriors be as hard as obsidian, and may their weapon hands be as nimble as the night wind itself. May they be as mighty as their ancestors, and may they be ever-victorious."

dialogues.speaker: Message
dialogues.text: "I picked up some sparkling clear shards while out on the road before. They didn't look like obsidian, but smelled like some kind of strange grain. There were these mysterious letters written onto them, too."

dialogues.speaker: Message
dialogues.text: "I think those are Cotan Grapes... or something like that. I've looked through the old classics, but never seen anything like that. Is anyone familiar with this sort of gemstone?"

dialogues.speaker: Another Person's Message
dialogues.text: "Where did you pick them up?"

dialogues.speaker: Message
dialogues.text: "Quite a ways off the beaten path, I think it was near the high priestess Citlali's residence...?"

dialogues.speaker: Another Person's Message
dialogues.text: "I see. This is something that causes people to lose their minds, talk nonsense, and even start dancing strange jigs. Its craftsmanship can be traced back to ancient times. Don't touch it... and don't drink it either."

dialogues.speaker: Message
dialogues.text: "What do you mean, 'don't drink it'? Anyway, if they're the High Priestess's ritual implements, I'd better return them to her."

dialogues.speaker: Granny Itztli's Message
dialogues.text: "No! Nope! Absolutely not! It's got nothing to do with me! Just find a random place and chuck it out!"

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "Children of the Masters of the Night-Wind — the long night wind has ceased, and the dark calamity has been cleansed."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "Now is the time for celebration and remembrance, to honor the heroes and warriors to whom we owe so much."

dialogues.speaker: Tribal Announcement
dialogues.text: "May the hero's path be straight and smooth. May the warrior's body be as unyielding obsidian. May the world never again face calamity's scourge. May peace last eternal as the Night Kingdom."

dialogues.speaker: Anonymous Message
dialogues.text: "Children of Mictlan, hear my voice."

dialogues.speaker: Anonymous Message
dialogues.text: #"Forging an Ancient Name is an arduous task, but earnest hearts shall grant {M#him}{F#her} their blessing."

dialogues.speaker: Anonymous Message
dialogues.text: "Each sacrifice will be acknowledged by the Wayob, every act of Devotion will be remembered by the Night Kingdom."

dialogues.speaker: Anonymous Message
dialogues.text: #"The memories of {M#his}{F#her} companions give {M#him}{F#her} {M#his}{F#her} name, and the traces of {M#his}{F#her} journey tell {M#his}{F#her} story."
